references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the sower: some fell on rocky ground where there was little soil, and it withered because it had no deep soil – corresponding to Luke's description of the seed that fell on rock and dried up due to lack of moisture.

Mark's parallel account of the parable of the sower: some fell on rocky ground where there was little soil, sprang up quickly, but was scorched by the sun and withered because it had no root – the same event as Luke 8:6.

Jesus' explanation of the seed on rocky ground in Matthew: it is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy, but has no root within and falls away when trouble comes – an exposition of what is described in Luke 8:6.
Jesus' explanation in Mark of the seed on rocky ground: they receive the word with joy, but have no root and fall away in times of trouble – a parallel to Luke's own explanation in 8:13.
Luke's own explanation of this verse: those on the rock are those who receive the word with joy, but they have no root and fall away in the time of testing.
Jeremiah describes the one who trusts in people as a bush in the wilderness, dwelling in dry desert places – an image reminiscent of the plant without moisture that dries up.
Ezekiel uses the image of a vine planted in dry soil that withers – parallel to the seed that dries up due to lack of moisture.
Psalm 1 contrasts the righteous as a tree planted by flowing water with the wicked who are like chaff – the image of having or lacking life-giving moisture is related to Luke 8:6.
Isaiah speaks of the grass that dries up and the flower that withers – a similar image of perishable growth without lasting vitality, just as the seed withered without moisture.
